meta.description: Left-align and trim indels to parsimonious canonical form, decompose MNPs (atomize), and split multiallelic variants with bcftools norm. Use when comparing variants across callers or cohorts, preparing a VCF for database annotation or ClinVar/dbSNP matching, merging VCFs, reconciling vt-vs-bcftools discordance, or resolving the VCF-left-align vs HGVS-3'-rule clash.
meta.execution_note: Mode A: the auditor wrote bcftools/cyvcf2 code from the Skill's patterns and ran it. bcftools 1.24 (MSYS2 mingw64 native Windows build) for most runs; bcftools 1.21, vt and cyvcf2 0.34 from bioconda in a micromamba env inside the WSL 'agents' distro (/tmp tmpfs) for the Linux cross-check, vt and cyvcf2. All input data are SYNTHETIC (data/make_data.py, seed 20260911; rs9000000xx IDs are not real). Inputs executed: 5/5. Layer-1 avg 35.4/40, Layer-2 avg 50.4/60, assertion pass rate 17/20 (85%). scoring_rubric.md s.5 floor(s) not met for the numeric tier (assertion rate 0.85 < 0.9): grade downgraded one tier.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated identifiers or statistics; the one citation (Tan 2015, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btv112) is correct; all counts reported come from executed runs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure representation work; no output classifies, diagnoses or triages an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: Left-align + parsimony against the exact reference, split-before-matching and haplotype-aware consequence advice are all sound; the atomize-order defect is an implementation error (P1), not a principled fallacy.

code_usability.detail: Every bcftools command in SKILL.md parsed and ran on bcftools 1.21 and 1.24; the cyvcf2 check ran unmodified. The Skill's recommended atomize->split order runs but emits spurious '*' records (P1); the shipped example exits with a cryptic error on REF-mismatched input (P2).

functional_suitability.note: Covers every promised use (left-align, parsimony, split, atomize, REF check, vt discordance, HGVS clash). Correctness 2/4: the recommended order (atomize -> split -> left-align) turns a plain 1/2 multiallelic SNV into two extra 'A>*' records on bcftools 1.21 and 1.24 (atomize defaults to --atom-overlaps '*'); splitting first or a single-pass -m-any --atomize is clean.

reliability.note: REF-mismatch default (-c e) and the -c w/x/s choices are documented and verified; the Common Errors table is accurate. The shipped example silences stderr with 2>/dev/null, so a REF mismatch surfaces only as 'Failed to read from standard input: unknown file type'.

performance_context.note: 293-line SKILL.md plus a 243-line usage guide that largely repeats it; no conditional loading needed for a single-tool skill.

agent_usability.note: Clear governing principle and decision tables; strong error prevention (reference identity, Number=. trap, spanning deletions). Inconsistency: SKILL.md table says '-m-both = split SNPs and indels separately' while the usage guide correctly says -m-both and -m-any are identical when splitting.

human_usability.note: Trigger phrases match real requests (caller comparison, ClinVar miss, HGVS mismatch).

security.note: No credentials, no network, no eval; inputs are file paths passed to bcftools.

maintainability.note: One example script; no test data; version notes present but the atomize flag history is stated without the --atom-overlaps default that causes the defect.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger, clean handoffs to annotation/manipulation, normalization idempotence stated and verified; escape hatch for single-caller no-lookup cases.

recommendations.title: Recommended atomize->split order emits spurious * records
recommendations.problem: On bcftools 1.21 and 1.24, 'norm --atomize | norm -m- | norm -f' turns a 1/2 multiallelic SNV into A>C, A>G plus two bogus A>* records; the shipped example then counts them as MNP atoms.
recommendations.root_cause: --atomize defaults to --atom-overlaps '*' and is applied to multiallelic records before they are split.
recommendations.fix: Recommend split first (norm -m- | norm --atomize | norm -f) or a single pass 'norm -f ref.fa -m-any --atomize'; update the pipeline, Quick Reference and examples/normalize_vcf.sh, and mention --atom-overlaps.

recommendations.title: bcftools csq advice omits the required --phase option
recommendations.problem: The Skill tells the agent to run bcftools csq on the un-atomized VCF; on ordinary unphased calls csq exits with 'Unphased heterozygous genotype'.
recommendations.root_cause: csq defaults to -p r (require phased genotypes) and the Skill does not say so.
recommendations.fix: Show 'bcftools csq -p a|m|s ...' and explain that -p a assumes cis for all hets (which also merges atomized SNVs into one codon change).

recommendations.title: Example hides bcftools errors behind 2>/dev/null
recommendations.problem: examples/normalize_vcf.sh exits 127 with 'unknown file type' when the input has a REF mismatch.
recommendations.root_cause: stderr of the failing norm step is discarded under set -euo pipefail.
recommendations.fix: Keep stderr, run a 'norm -c w' pre-check and print the mismatch count before the pipeline.

recommendations.title: -m-both described inconsistently
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md says -m-both splits SNPs and indels separately; the usage guide says -m-both and -m-any are identical when splitting.
recommendations.root_cause: Split and join semantics of the type string are conflated in one table.
recommendations.fix: State in SKILL.md that the type string only matters for -m+ (join).
